title: fix: unblock fresh Windows state initialization
body:
Fixes #176163.

## What Problem This Solves

Fresh Windows installs can reject onboarding, Doctor, and Gateway startup as “undergoing offline maintenance” even though the command holds its own schema lease.

## User Impact

State initialization keeps its maintenance authority when Windows path spelling changes. A missing same-process scope now produces a typed internal ownership error with retry/report guidance; real foreign maintenance still refuses access.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process-owner registry and schema scope were keyed by the lock pathname. Native realpath can change that pathname's spelling after directory creation, leaving the live scope unreachable while the persisted lock still identifies this PID. Both registries now use one canonical database identity, including Windows case and namespace normalization. Owners retain their acquired physical lock paths, and captured handles carry their prepared identity.

The existing on-disk lock names and hashes are unchanged, preserving exclusion with older processes. Contention errors now live beside the other ownership errors; the existing import surface is retained. No config, dependency, schema, or lock-protocol change is required. The ownership path uses built-in filesystem and AsyncLocalStorage operations; npm install scripts do not create or register its schema scopes.

## Evidence

- The new real-lease regression failed before the key fix in the same-process persisted-owner assertion, then passed while initializing an actual SQLite database. Windows path simulations cover case, forward slashes, extended-length prefixes, short names, and first creation; a distinct profile retains a distinct key.
- Focused owner proof: 26 tests passed. Expanded diagnostic/consumer proof: 18 files, 287 tests passed. Existing same-process refusal assertions now expect the internal diagnostic; foreign-owner assertions retain the offline-maintenance contract.
- The required 113 direct/one-barrel consumer test files were all exercised (963.7 s total). The initial run had three old-message expectation failures in chat identity, worker admission, and Doctor admission. Their corrected suites passed in the focused reruns; no unrelated functional failures remained. No individual test exceeded 30 s; the largest per-file test total was 90.8 s in the existing Doctor schema-guard suite.
- Core and infrastructure-test TypeScript checks, changed-file oxlint and oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and the import-cycle check passed (0 cycles). The full SQLite inventory scan was omitted for host runtime cost. The changed-test graph selector hit inherited root-budget excesses (gateway 730/720; infrastructure 743/720, including this new test); direct compiler checks were used instead.
- Independent P1 review found no remaining actionable findings. Production LOC: +99/-63; test LOC: +134/-22; docs: +6.

Live local proof used isolated HOME/state directories, a fresh profile, and free loopback port 63838:

```sh
HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/live-home-final" \
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PWD/.artifacts/live-state-proof" \
TMPDIR="$PWD/.artifacts/tmp" \
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=63838 OPENCLAW_FORCE_BUILD=1 \
pnpm dev --profile l1686-proof doctor --non-interactive

HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/live-home-final" \
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PWD/.artifacts/live-state-proof" \
TMPDIR="$PWD/.artifacts/tmp" OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=63838 \
pnpm dev --profile l1686-proof gateway run --allow-unconfigured --bind loopback --port 63838

curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:63838/healthz
# {"ok":true,"status":"live"}
```

Doctor completed after a successful runtime build. Gateway schema preflight passed, startup reached ready, and the owned Gateway shut down cleanly after SIGINT (127 ms). Doctor emitted the existing optional memory-system warning. Native Windows execution remains a CI/platform proof gap; Windows semantics were simulated locally, and no remote lease was used.
